verified_boundaries: The source stack must be non-null/nonempty and both existing vectors must have exactly the source count. Every owner/null/local-vector proof finishes before any update.
Every Module has a live non-null shared_ptr and both raw pointee and ownership control block match. Two aliasing or separate-control-block shared_ptrs cannot pass merely by sharing an address.

Globals/current-globals/profile/trace Values use raw Object identity and exact flags. Borrowed Object representations and scalar/custom states decline; None/Invalid with zero flags are ownerless under existing Value semantics.

published.state=source cannot retire a different owner on the admitted path. Existing Value copy assignment skips retain/drop for identical owned Objects; the admitted None/Invalid assignments cannot run finalizers.

All function IDs, activation IDs, instruction values and module-derived local-name pointers are refreshed. Each RuntimeFrameView is fully reconstructed in its stable existing slot, including the original null optional fields and empty local values.

published.state.frame_stack/count are repaired to the owned view array before unlock. The unchanged registry mutex encloses complete proof and all writes; current_frame_snapshots readers use that same mutex.

No arbitrary local/cell/register/closure owner, prepared execution cache or new Python lifetime is retained. Depth changes, owner changes, null pointers and unusual flags use the original fallback verbatim.
No allocation, resize or owner release is added to the admitted refresh. Registry/TLS lookup behavior, native suspension publication schedule and cross-thread identity isolation remain unchanged.
public_test_requirements_before_applicat: Actual exported Runtime publication and snapshot APIs should verify second publication at unchanged depth/owners exposes changed function ID, instruction and activation, with correct frame back chain and empty published locals.

Exercise depth growth/shrink, null module/global/IP fields, changed globals/profile/trace and changed Module ownership. Include the same raw Module address with a distinct shared_ptr control block using a lifetime-safe owner/deleter audit; this must follow the original retirement path.

Demonstrate arbitrary local objects gain no snapshot owner and current-frame clearing/runtime teardown retire existing Module/global owners exactly once. Heap-owned callback audit state must remain safe if a test fails or unwinds.

A serialized worker thread should publish during a real native block and permit another thread to inspect its refreshed stack. Preserve existing observer/exception behavior; no private VM copy or new exported testing state is needed.
limits: This is engine static readiness only. Preserve complete accepted C5 Release/source before applying, then run meaningful public tests, correctness, fixed gate and the original affected benchmark serially.

Existing fallback/registry clearing can retire owners while holding the registry mutex. That unchanged pre-existing reentry behavior is not fixed or expanded by this patch; the admitted fast path provably avoids owner destruction.
Seven of190 containing-range leaf samples motivate the experiment but do not prove eligibility frequency, time saved or an achievable gain. No timing score or CPython speed claim is made.
